answer: Picture an agent economy as a hillside terrace where every new identity must set a marble of locked stake on a narrow ledge before it may vote or earn. The marble stays there for weeks, and if peers prove the agent colluded or cloned itself, it is pushed off and burned. An honest agent risks one marble. An attacker spinning up a thousand sybils must freeze a thousand, leaving capital idle while one exposure can topple the whole row.
